chapter: The Vitaphone film and studio work
title: The Follies Theater revue format and Lawrence Welk comparison
summary: At the Follies the band played each week with changing visiting performers, a format like Lawrence Welk's show, with Spikes as emcee and bandleader.

bands.name: Reb Spikes and His Majors and Minors Orchestra

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And was this a show similar to what you were doing at The Follies, or was this a show put together for...
Yeah, about the same thing we was doing at The Follies.
Was it the same performers, or were there different performers?

Well, yeah, you know, we had...at The Follies, we had new performers every week. All the old colored performers that would come in town nearly we'd use them a week or so, you know, at The Follies in our act. But our band went on every week. We did a different number--maybe some novelty or somethin'--and then we had the entertainers, and we played for the entertainers right in the middle. Just like Lawrence Welk is today.

One of the things you were telling me on the telephone was that the format of this film that you made for Warner Bros. was almost identical to what Lawrence Welk's Show is on television now--the band and then specialty acts.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. And he announces them, and I announced them and everything, you know.
So you were the emcee and the leader of the band in the film.
